        "title": "task-baf873fe: aligned-marker gap filling and validation",
        "content": "Continual-ARC task-baf873fe: validated rule and execution caution.\n\nRule: identify the sparse marker color in the current grid (do not hard-code a hue; across this task’s demos markers were 0, 9, 4, 1, and 5, while the dominant/corner background varied). For each row and each column, find consecutive positions occupied by that marker. Recolor only original background cells strictly between each consecutive aligned marker pair to color 3. Preserve marker endpoints and all cells outside those spans. Apply row and column fills independently, based on the original input, and take their union.\n\nEvidence: demos consistently show straight horizontal/vertical gap fill, no diagonal fill, no extension beyond the outer markers, and preserve marker cells. Examples include demo8: color-5 markers at (r0,c0) and (r6,c0) fill r1–r5 in c0; row2 markers c1 and c5 fill c2–c4. Demo6 row0 marker-0 positions c3,c5,c8,c13,c16 fill the intervening 9s. Test palette can change: solved test had 0 markers and 1 background; output filled only intervening 1s with 3.\n\nImportant error-prevention lesson: do not manually retype the test grid into a separate variable without checking it against the prompt. In the failed attempt on the solved 22x18 input, row index 4 had columns 10 and 11 transposed in the manually entered grid (the true zeros were at c11 and c17, not c10 and c17, while c10 was 1). This caused multiple otherwise-rule-correct submissions to fail. Parse the exact current input, verify every row has the stated width, and compare it back to the source before computing. Generate the JSON output from the computed array rather than hand-copying: a later manual transcription also flipped one output cell (r6,c7). The final correct submission was obtained by reparsing the exact prompt grid, applying the rule programmatically, and submitting the generated grid.",

        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "Continual-ARC task-0c1f1b2f: extrapolate periodic stripe patterns",
        "content": "For Continual-ARC task-0c1f1b2f, stripe clues encode a periodic color pattern to expand across the whole grid. Full horizontal stripes specify colors at row coordinates; infer a simple row-wise cycle and preserve its phase from the input coordinates. Diagonal stripe markers specify colors by diagonal coordinate: use r-c for down-right diagonals and r+c for the opposite slope, then extend the inferred cycle across the grid. Do not leave unmarked cells blank. Infer the period from all marker positions and colors, not from palette or spacing alone; repeated colors may occupy multiple phases. Validate that the proposed cycle reproduces every marked stripe before submitting. Verified test: parallel r-c diagonals at 5 and 10 had colors 5 and 6, respectively; the consistent period-2 field was color 6 on even r-c and color 5 on odd r-c, and submission was correct. Demonstrations included horizontal periodic sequences and diagonal periodic patterns with other periods, so do not assume period 2 universally.",

        "id": "task_3a935ce0_diagonal_periodic_wallpaper",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "Continual-ARC task-3a935ce0: infer periodic wallpaper from clue geometry",
        "content": "For Continual-ARC task-3a935ce0, sparse nonzero cells are clues encoding a periodic color pattern; zeros are blank/background, not clues. First identify clue geometry and choose the periodic coordinate that matches it. For horizontal full-row stripes, map each nonzero uniform row by its zero-based row index modulo the wallpaper period; fill zero rows with the color of their matching residue. Include every nonzero hue as a clue even if it is 9 (the background hue can differ by instance). Infer a period supported by all clue rows and use available pattern evidence rather than assuming the smallest conflict-free period is always intended. Validated case: the 9×9 input rows were [5,0,2,1,9,9,9,0,9], where 0 denotes a blank row. The accepted output rows were [5,9,2,1,9,9,9,5,9], corresponding to period 7 and row-color cycle [5,9,2,1,9,9,9] indexed from row 0; the clues at rows 0,2,3,4,5,6,8 all agree, and blank rows 1 and 7 fill to 9 and 5. In another validated 17×17 case, clues at row indices 1, 3, 4, 6, 8, and 11 implied period 6 and row-color sequence [8,4,5,1,4,5] starting at row 0; a demo confirmed the period-6 repetition. For diagonal clues, infer the corresponding diagonal residue mapping and tile the grid. Validate that every clue is reproduced and every output row has exactly the input width; malformed dimensions invalidate the grid.",

        "title": "Continual-ARC task-a851f6ef: arrange four rotated copies in quadrants",

The 3×3 validation input [[5,7,2],[0,3,6],[9,8,1]] produced [[5,7,2,9,0,5],[0,3,6,8,3,7],[9,8,1,1,6,2],[2,6,1,1,8,9],[7,3,8,6,3,0],[5,0,9,2,7,5]].         "content": "For Continual-ARC task-73ff91f3, identify the regular horizontal and vertical lattice lines from the current input, and infer the ordinary separator color and panel interior/background color. Restrict the reduced output to the lattice span containing non-separator clue intersections: exclude outer blank lattice rows or columns and trailing blank panels. Four equal separator-color corners do not qualify as a marker match; output the interior/background color instead.\n\nAdditional accepted 30×28 validation: horizontal lattice lines r=1,14,27 and vertical lines c=0,13,26; separator 4 and panel interior 3.         "content": "For Continual-ARC task-e0e0ff3d, identify each complete hollow, axis-aligned square frame with intact, uniform-color borders. Preserve its outline and fill every interior cell uniformly: use color 2 when the outer side length is even and color 7 when it is odd. Derive frame bounds and side lengths from the current input; do not assume fixed positions or outline colors. Preserve all non-interior cells. Validated across accepted inputs, including an exact no-demo 18×19 case with frames at zero-indexed top-left positions (0,13) and (3,6), each side 5; (8,13), side 4; and (12,6), side 3. The accepted output filled the side-5 and side-3 interiors with 7 and the side-4 interior with 2, preserving all frame borders and background. Before submission, check each frame's bounds, completeness, parity, interior fill, and preservation of every other cell.\n\nAdditional accepted fresh validation (11×18, one wrong submission before correction): frames at zero-indexed top-left positions (1,0), side 3; (6,1), side 4; and (0,6), side 8. Fill only strict interior coordinates r0+1..r0+side-2 and c0+1..c0+side-2. A failed first attempt came from placing the side-3 fill in the row above its true interior; explicitly derive interior bounds from the frame's top and bottom borders before editing.
